requiresNavigation.description: Whether TASK requests additional document acquisition beyond this starting document.

resultFlow.description: Declared result-processing flow reference, or null for selected page data and references only.

preconditions.description: Context selector/count checks applied to every supplied page before result and navigation selection. An empty array adds no context checks.

selector.description: CSS selecting current-page result elements, or null for no result selection. Selecting an anchor returns its data; result controls resource fetching.

links.description: CSS selecting link elements for next-stage document acquisition, or null for no onward navigation. Independent from current-page result selection.

fields.description: Optional structured fields with arbitrary names, scoped to each selected result record. Null or omission returns ordinary native elements. Requires a non-null result selector.

result.description: Optional processing of selected results: a bundled flow reference and a property path to each resource URL. Null means no result-processing flow for this stage.

selector.description: XPath 1.0 selecting the record elements in source order.

namespaces.description: XPath prefix to namespace URI bindings. Use explicit bindings for namespaced elements, including a source default namespace; XPath prefixes need not match source prefixes. Use {} for unnamespaced XML. The reserved __proto__ record key is unsupported.

fields.description: Arbitrary field names mapped to XPath 1.0 expressions evaluated relative to each selected element. string(...) returns a scalar string, boolean(...) a boolean; node-set expressions return all their string values as an array. The reserved __proto__ record key is unsupported.

selector.description: CSS identifying page context checked before result and navigation selection.

maximum.description: Inclusive maximum context matches; null means unbounded. Must be at least minimum.

anyOf.description: Arbitrary field names mapped to record-scoped CSS/read/bounds rules. Values remain arrays. The reserved __proto__ field key is unsupported.

selector.description: CSS over this record and its descendants only, in document order. :scope explicitly selects the record itself.

attribute.description: Null reads native text; a name reads that exact parsed HTML attribute, not a JavaScript property name. Missing attributes produce null, not invented text.

minimum.description: Inclusive minimum selected elements per record. Zero permits no matches. This counts elements, not non-null or nonempty values.

maximum.description: Inclusive maximum selected elements per record; null is unbounded.

reference.description: Property path within each selected item to its resource URL, for example ["attributes","href"] for an anchor or ["attributes","content"] for URL metadata.

AI Summit (Virtual) - Run AI and Data PipelinesWed, Nov 4 · 4:00 PM CET·OnlineOnlineImportant: Register on the event website to receive the joining link. (rsvp on meetup will NOT receive anything).
Building the prototype is the easy part. Keeping it running, with fresh data, tested agents, and pipelines that don’t need babysitting, is where most teams get stuck.
Airflow Summit Online Reconnect brings engineers from Waze, Notion, Uber and more to show how they actually do it. It’s free, 100% virtual, and built for developers, data engineers and AI practitioners.
What you’ll see:

Waze: one platform for data and MLOps, 400+ pipelines, and AI-driven optimizations that cut BigQuery workloads by up to 95%.
Notion: how a small team runs a data platform across four regions and a fleet of agents.
Uber: shipping DAGs like microservices, with version pinning and automated rollback.
Who judges the agents? An automated eval platform that took a team from monthly releases to two or more per week.
RAG at scale: keeping millions of documents parsed, embedded and indexed with Airflow and Apache Beam.

🎁 Attend and you’re in the draw for an official Airflow certification exam from Astronomer, gift cards and other prizes.
Featured Speakers:

Abdul Majid Mohammed, Sr Specialist Solutions Architect @ AWS
Alex Ohayon, Google - Engineering Manager, Data Infrastructure, Waze
Ashir Alam, Sr Data Engineer at Credit Karma
Piyush Maheshwari, Sr Software Engineer at Uber
Ramzi Alashabi, Chapter Lead Data and Streaming @ ABNAMRO Bank
Sean Bjurstrom, Sr Specialist Solutions Architect, Analytics @ AWS
Sneha Rao, Senior Solutions Architect @ AWS
Yunhao Qing, Senior SWE @ Notion Data Platform

Venue:
Virtual, join from anywhere5 attendees

Google AI Deep Dive (Ep 5) - Discriminative (Jev/DiffusionGemma) modelsWed, Nov 11 · 6:00 PM CET·OnlineOnlineImportant: Register on the event website to receive the joining link. (rsvp on meetup will NOT receive anything).
This is virtual event for our AI global community, please double-check your local time. Can't make it live? Register anyway to receive the webinar recording.
The AI Deep Dive Series is a hands-on virtual initiative designed to empower developers to architect the next generation of Agentic AI. Moving beyond basic prompting, this series guides you through the complete engineering lifecycle using Google’s advanced stack.
You will master the transition from local Gemini CLI environments to building intelligent agents with the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and Model Context Protocol (MCP), culminating in the deployment of secure, collaborative Agent-to-Agent (A2A) ecosystems on Google Cloud Run. Join us to build AI systems that can truly reason, act, and scale.
Workshop: Getting started with Discriminative (Jev/DiffusionGemma) models
Speaker: Christina Lin (Google)
Venue:
Virtual, join from anywhere
More virtual sessions:
